title: The Great Carrot Rescue
markdown:
The Giggleberry Vegetable Show smelled of warm pies and pure silliness. Giant pumpkins sat like houses. Cabbages puffed like green clouds. Leeks stretched as if they meant to tickle the moon. In the middle of all that, Acorn the squirrel’s bushy tail did a jig, and Wisp the ferret’s nose twitched toward trouble, and possibly cheese. They were partners in fun, always.

“Acorn, look,” Wisp squeaked, pointing. “Mayor Marmalade’s carrot.”

This was not just any carrot. This was the Giggleberry Grand Prize, huge, sunset-coloured, leafy crown like a green hat. And it was wobbling on the edge of the Sparkling Fountain, one nudge from a long wet disastrous dive.

“A watery carrot catastrophe,” Acorn said, whiskers quivering. “Think of the lost giggles.”

But the guards were two men dressed as giant stern turnips, faces like swallowed lemons, and the crowds were thick as jam. Therefore they could not simply stroll up and shove.

Acorn’s eyes lit as if he had found a secret nut. “We’ll sneak. Like furry shadows on a windy day.”

They darted through zucchinis longer than school buses. The turnip-men were busy admiring a beetroot that looked like a grumpy old man’s face. “Hurry, Wisp.”

Wisp wriggled under a pie table. Acorn scampered over it and nearly tripped on a rogue string bean. Guard Goose Number One, looking terribly cross, honked a honk of pure annoyance.

But the goose had seen them. Therefore they needed a distraction.

Acorn leaped onto a giant bright red strawberry. It was enormous. It rolled. Guard Goose Number One, bewildered, honked again and waddled off to chase the runaway fruit, webbed feet slapping pie crumbs.

Now it was just the carrot, the fountain, and a tiny bit of distance. Wisp pushed, little legs churning. Acorn scrambled up the leafy crown and pulled with nimble paws. The giant carrot teetered. It groaned like a wooden ship.

It almost went in. Water kissed the tip. Therefore they heaved together: Wisp’s last shove, Acorn’s squeaky tug. The carrot lurched back and settled with a soft thud, far from the splash.

Mayor Marmalade, a portly fellow with a cheerful radish face, rushed over. “My carrot. It’s safe. Who saved it?”

Acorn and Wisp, misted from the fountain and a bit dusty, peeked from behind a giant sunflower. They were small. Their bravery was not. The Mayor scooped them up gently.

“My heroes.” He did not stop at thanks. He presented a whole bushel of juicy giggleberries, bursting with flavour, enough to stain two sets of whiskers pink. The turnip-guards clapped, which made their costumes wobble. The goose returned with a strawberry and no explanation.

Acorn and Wisp sat on the prize carrot’s safe side of the fountain and ate berries until their tummies felt like festivals. What a day. What a vegetable. What a very silly, very important rescue.
